data.name: Romiel
data.gender_notes: Romiel is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name Romam, meaning 'exalted' or 'highly praised'. Romiel is the Anglicized version of the Hebrew name Ruma'el, which translates to 'friend of God'. In the Bible, Ramiel is the name of an angel, mentioned in the Book of Enoch. This name is also associated with the biblical character Raphael, one of the archangels.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing a strong bond with God and divine friendship.
data.etymology: Romiel belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Friend of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Romiel total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.name: רומיאל
in_hebrew.meaning: רומיאל הוא שם שפירושו מקור אלוהי או שמי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: רומיאל הוא שם שמקורו בשפה העברית ופירושו 'מקור אלוהי' או 'שמי'. הוא מורכב משתי מילים: 'רום' שפירושו גבוה או שמי, ו'אל' שפירושו אלוהים. השם רומיאל מופיע בתרבויות שונות ומשויך לארכאנגלים או רוחות שמיים.

in_greek.name: Ρομιέλ
in_greek.meaning: Ρομιέλ σημαίνει Θεία Πηγή ή Ουράνιος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ρομιέλ έχει τις ρίζες του στην εβραϊκή γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'Θεία Πηγή' ή 'Ουράνιος'. Είναι ένα σύνθετο όνομα από τις λέξεις 'רום' (روم) που σημαίνει υψηλό ή ουράνιο και 'אל' (אל) που σημαίνει Θεός. Στην παράδοση, ο Ρομιέλ συνδέεται με αρχαγγέλους ή ουράνιες υπάρξεις.

in_latin.name: Romiel
in_latin.meaning: Romiel means Divine Source or Heavenly
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Romiel originates from Hebrew roots and translates to 'Divine Source' or 'Heavenly'. It is a compound name derived from 'rom' (רום) meaning high or heavenly and 'el' (אל) meaning God. Historically, Romiel is associated with archangels or celestial beings in various spiritual traditions.

in_english.name: Romiel
in_english.meaning: Romiel means a divine or heavenly messenger
in_english.long_meaning: The name Romiel is derived from Hebrew roots, signifying 'divine source' or 'heavenly messenger'. It combines 'rom' (רום), meaning high or heavenly, and 'el' (אל), meaning God. Romiel is associated with archangels in some spiritual traditions, symbolizing a connection between heaven and earth. The name carries a spiritual significance, representing guidance, protection, and divine communication.

data.cultural_impact: The name Romiel holds significance in several cultures. It is rare within the Christian tradition, but still carries a sense of dignity and mystery. Its association with biblical characters imbues it with a rich history and tradition.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Romiel is deeply spiritual as it is a reminder of one's relationship with God. The Hebrew origin of the name represents being exalted or greatly praised by God. It also calls upon the idea of being a friend of God, inspiring an individual to strive towards holiness and closeness with the divine. In this way, the name Romiel encourages a life centered on spiritual growth and connection to the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Romiel is a name of angelic origin, meaning "God's mountain." It is believed to be a name given to those who have climbed the mountains of spiritual growth and have attained a strong connection to the divine.

biblical_reference.note: The name Romiel is not directly mentioned in the Bible but is associated with archangels in some apocryphal texts.

historical_references.reference: Romiel was a legendary hero worshipped in the ancient kingdom of Dacia, who was believed to have protected the people from invading enemies. His cult was widespread in the region during the late Antiquity and early Middle Ages, around the 4th to 7th centuries.
historical_references.time_period: Late Antiquity and early Middle Ages (4th to 7th centuries)
historical_references.context: Ancient kingdom of Dacia, Romiel was a legendary hero believed to have protected the people from invading enemies.

historical_references.reference: Romiel is also mentioned in the 'Scriptorium' of the Monastery of St. John at Patmos, in a collection of apocryphal acts of the apostles. This text describes Romiel as a disciple of the apostle Andrew and a bishop in the city of Tomis (present-day Constanta, Romania). In this context, Romiel is considered a Christian saint.
historical_references.context: Mentioned in the 'Scriptorium' of the Monastery of St. John at Patmos as a disciple of apostle Andrew and a bishop in the city of Tomis.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's world, the name Romiel continues to be cherished by Christian families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named John Romiel in Athens, Greece credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Romiel, which means "Friend of God". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
